helvetia: Swiss Public Statistics, Regional Classifications and Spatial Data

Source: R/helvetia-package.R
helvetia-package.Rd

helvetia gives a small, stable API to official Swiss sources and maps them to one historicisable data model. The functions fall into six groups:

Registers – which units exist at a given date:

FunctionPurposeKey
gemeinde()municipalities valid at a date (AGVCH)stand_d + gem_id
gemeindeMutationen()mergers, splits, renamings (AGVCH)mutation_id + old/new version
raumgliederung()spatial classifications (AGVCH)stand_d + gem_id + typ_c
praemienregion()health insurance premium regions (BAG)jahr_n + gem_id + preg_c
kanton()cantons with numbers and nameskanton_id

Statistics – values per municipality:

FunctionPurposeKey
popGemeinde()population by sex and age (STATPOP)jahr_n + gem_stand_d + gem_id + sex_c + age_n
arealGemeinde()land use (Arealstatistik)period_x + gem_stand_d + gem_id + noas_c
noas()NOAS04 nomenclaturenoas_c

Geometries – polygons and points:

FunctionPurpose
geoGemeinde(), geoBezirk(), geoKanton()institutional boundaries
geoThemakart()any ThemaKart layer, incl. vegetation area and label points
geoGewaesser()lakes and rivers
themakartSets()available ThemaKart sets

Maps (formerly bfsMaps): plotMap(), addGewaesser(), stampBfs().

Spatial tools: combineRegions(), neighbours(), locate(), geocode().

Sources: sourceInfo(), cacheList(), cacheClear().

Column names encode the type by suffix: _id identifiers, _x text, _c codes, _n numbers, _d dates, _l logicals. Register stands (stand_d), statistical years (jahr_n), survey periods (period_x) and boundary stands (gem_stand_d) are never mixed: a bare gem_id is not sufficient for historical analyses. The column names follow the attribute conventions of the source databases and are therefore in snake_case, unlike function arguments and list components, which are lowerCamelCase.
